texts.error.no_battery: This cartridge has no battery-backed memory, so it keeps no saved games, and '%1' would not be read.
texts.error.no_bsx_bios: This is a Satellaview file, and it needs the Satellaview's BIOS (%1), which was not given.
texts.error.no_coleco_bios: The ColecoVision needs its BIOS (%1), which was not given.
texts.error.no_fds_bios: This is a Famicom Disk System disk, and it needs the Disk System's BIOS (disksys.rom), which was not given.
texts.error.no_file: No cartridge file is in the project.
texts.error.no_gba_bios: The Game Boy Advance needs its BIOS (%1), which was not given.
texts.error.no_pce_card: A PC Engine CD disc needs the program of the card in the console's slot (%1), which was not given.
texts.error.no_sgb_bios: The Super Game Boy needs the program of its cartridge (%1), which was not given.
texts.error.no_snes_chip: This cartridge has a chip that runs a program of its own, and that program's file (%1) was not given.
texts.error.no_sufami_bios: This is a Sufami Turbo cartridge, and it needs the Sufami Turbo's BIOS (%1), which was not given.
texts.error.not_cue: '%1' is not a disc's .cue file. A PC Engine CD game is given by its .cue file, with the files it names beside it.
texts.error.not_machine: Mesen did not load '%1' as a game for the console this project is for. Check the Console setting.
texts.error.not_nes: '%1' is not an NES game. This core runs NES games only.
texts.firmware.bsx.about: The program of the BS-X cartridge, which the Satellaview (a satellite receiver for the Super Famicom) starts from. It is needed for a Satellaview file (.bs).
texts.firmware.cgb_boot.about: Nintendo's program that the Game Boy Color runs when it is switched on, before the game (2304 bytes). It is needed when Boot ROM is Nintendo's.
texts.firmware.coleco_bios.about: The 8 KB program inside the ColecoVision, which starts every cartridge and which games call for some of their work. Mesen needs it for every ColecoVision game.
texts.firmware.dmg_boot.about: Nintendo's program that the Game Boy runs when it is switched on, before the game (256 bytes). It is needed when Boot ROM is Nintendo's.
texts.firmware.fds_bios.about: The 8 KB program inside the Famicom Disk System's adapter, which starts every disk. It is needed for a Disk System game (.fds).
texts.firmware.gba_bios.about: The 16 KB program inside the Game Boy Advance, which starts every game and which games call for some of their work. Mesen needs it for every Game Boy Advance game; only a program made to need no BIOS runs without it (BIOS: None).
texts.firmware.gecard.about: The program on the Games Express card, which goes into the PC Engine for the discs Games Express made (32 KB). Mesen needs it for those discs instead of the System Card.
texts.firmware.sc_boot.about: Bandai's program that the SwanCrystal runs when it is switched on, before the game (8 KB). It is needed when Boot ROM is on and the console model is the SwanCrystal.
texts.firmware.sgb1.about: The Super NES program on the Super Game Boy cartridge (256 KB). It is needed when the Super Game Boy Model is Super Game Boy.
texts.firmware.sgb2.about: The Super NES program on the Super Game Boy 2 cartridge (512 KB). It is needed when the Super Game Boy Model is Super Game Boy 2.
texts.firmware.sgb2_boot.about: Nintendo's program that the Super Game Boy 2's Game Boy runs when it is switched on (256 bytes). It is needed when Boot ROM is Nintendo's.
texts.firmware.sgb_boot.about: Nintendo's program that the Super Game Boy's Game Boy runs when it is switched on (256 bytes). It is needed when Boot ROM is Nintendo's.
texts.firmware.sms_bios_japan.about: The program inside the console that shows the Sega logo and then starts the cartridge (8 KB). It is needed when Master System BIOS is this one.
texts.firmware.sms_bios_usa.about: The program inside the console that shows the Sega logo and then starts the cartridge (8 KB). It is needed when Master System BIOS is this one.
texts.firmware.snes_chip.about: The program inside a chip on this game's cartridge. Mesen needs a copy of it to run the game.
texts.firmware.sufami.about: The program of the Sufami Turbo, an adapter for the Super Famicom that holds two small cartridges. It is needed for a Sufami Turbo cartridge (.st).
texts.firmware.syscard3.about: The program on the card that goes into the PC Engine for its CD drive (256 KB), which starts every CD game. Mesen uses version 3.0, the Super CD-ROM System, for every PC Engine CD game.
texts.firmware.ws_boot.about: Bandai's program that the WonderSwan runs when it is switched on, before the game (4 KB). It is needed when Boot ROM is on.
texts.firmware.wsc_boot.about: Bandai's program that the WonderSwan Color runs when it is switched on, before the game (8 KB). It is needed when Boot ROM is on. Only when the console model is the WonderSwan Color (the SwanCrystal has its own).
texts.firmware.ymf288.about: The 8 KB of drum sounds inside the YM2608 and YMF288 sound chips, which the EPSM's drums play. It is the same data as the file ym2608_adpcm_rom.bin. It is needed only when EPSM Drums is On.
texts.setting.boot_rom.about: The program the Game Boy runs when it is switched on, before the game: Mesen's own (free, written for the SameBoy emulator) or Nintendo's, which you give as firmware. They take different times, so it is part of the machine, and a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.epsm_drums.about: The EPSM is a sound chip some new games for the NES use. Its drums play sounds kept in the chip's own memory, and Mesen needs a copy of that memory, the YMF288 rhythm ROM, to play them. On asks for that file. Off plays the drums silent. The game's music and sound effects play either way. It changes the sound only.
texts.setting.expansion.about: What is plugged into the expansion port on the front of the Famicom, the Japanese console. The Famicom Zapper and the Famicom Arkanoid controller are the Japanese versions of the Zapper and the Arkanoid controller. The four-player adapter holds four controllers, for Japanese games made for four players. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value. EPSM is the EPSM sound chip, for a game made for it whose header does not say so. A game whose NES 2.0 header asks for the EPSM has it whatever this says. The Family Trainer is the same mat made for the Famicom; Konami's Hyper Shot is two pairs of buttons (Run and Jump) for its sports games; the Party Tap holds six players' buttons, for quiz games. The two-player adapter holds two controllers. The Oeka Kids tablet is a drawing tablet with a pen; the Family BASIC keyboard (72 keys) and the Subor keyboard (99 keys) are computer keyboards; the Pachinko controller has a knob, turned by holding one of its two buttons; the Famicom Network System controller has number keys; the Exciting Boxing punching bag and the Jissen Mahjong controller were each made for one game; the Hori Track is a trackball; the Hyper Shot made by Bandai is a light gun with a controller.
texts.setting.expansion.bandai_hyper_shot: Hyper Shot (Bandai, light gun with a controller)
texts.setting.gba_bios.about: Nintendo's BIOS is firmware you give, and every commercial game needs it: games call it for some of their work. None runs without it, for a program made to need no BIOS (a test program, or homebrew that calls none of its functions and turns on no interrupt); the boot screen is then always skipped, and a game that calls the BIOS stops. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.gba_skip_boot.about: On starts the game at once, in the state the BIOS would leave the console in, without the Game Boy Advance logo (Mesen's option of the same name, off by default in Mesen). Off shows the logo first, as the console does. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.machine.about: Which console this project is for. Mesen emulates each of these. A project made before this setting existed is an NES project. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.nes_model.about: Which NES or Famicom the game runs on: the NES (NES-001), its later top-loading model (NES-101), the Famicom (HVC-001) or the AV Famicom (HVC-101). Mesen tells them apart only by what a read of the controller ports finds on the lines no device drives, and, on the Famicom HVC-001, by a read of the controllers that the sound chip interrupts reaching the controller twice. Almost every game plays the same on all four. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.pce_cd_type.about: Which card is in the console for its CD drive: the Arcade Card (the default, which plays every disc), the Super CD-ROM System, or the first CD-ROM System, which has less memory: a disc made for more memory does not run with it. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.pce_model.about: The Japanese PC Engine or the American TurboGrafx-16. A game from one region checks which console it is on. Auto lets Mesen choose from the game. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.pce_pad.about: The controllers in the port, or in the multitap: the usual two-button controller, or NEC's Avenue Pad 6, which adds the buttons III, IV, V and VI for the games made for six buttons. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.pce_port.about: What is plugged into the console's one controller port: a controller, nothing, or a multitap (the TurboTap), which holds five controllers for games made for more players. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.port1.about: What is plugged into the console's first controller port. The Four Score takes both ports and holds four controllers, for games made for four players; the second port is then not used. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value. The Super NES controller, the Super NES Mouse and the NTT Data Keypad (a Super NES controller with number keys) are read by some new games; the Subor mouse is the mouse of the Subor computers; the Virtual Boy controller has two direction pads.
texts.setting.port2.about: What is plugged into the console's second controller port. The Zapper is the light gun; the Arkanoid controller is a knob with one button, made for the game Arkanoid. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value. The Power Pad is a floor mat of twelve squares, numbered on each of its two sides. The Famicom second controller has a microphone, which some Famicom games listen to. The other devices are the same as in the first port.
texts.setting.ram.about: What the console's memory holds when it is switched on. A real console starts with values nobody chose, and a few games behave differently because of them. Random fills it from the Random Seed below. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.region.about: Which console the game runs on: an American or Japanese NTSC NES (60 frames a second), a European PAL NES (50), or a Dendy (the Russian clone, 50). Auto takes the cartridge's header or Mesen's game database. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.rtc_start.about: The date and time a clock in the cartridge (or the Satellaview's) shows when the game starts. The clock then moves with the game's own time, not the computer's. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.seed.about: The number the random values start from, when Memory at Power On is Random. The same number gives the same values every time. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sgb_model.about: The first Super Game Boy, or the Super Game Boy 2 sold in Japan, whose Game Boy runs at the speed of a real Game Boy. Each needs its own cartridge program as firmware. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sms_bios.about: Off starts the cartridge at once, as Mesen does by default. The American or the Japanese BIOS shows Sega's logo first and then starts it, as the console does; each is firmware you give. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sms_fm.about: The FM Sound Unit, a sound chip (Yamaha YM2413) that the Japanese Master System has and that some games play their music on. Mesen plugs it in by default. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sms_model.about: Mesen's Compatibility (its default), the first Master System or the Master System 2. They differ in what a read of an unused port finds, and in how the video chip reads its name table when a game leaves one of its bits clear: the first Master System then repeats the top of the name table at the bottom of the picture. Almost every game plays the same on all three. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sms_port1.about: What is plugged into the console's first controller port: a controller, or the Light Phaser, Sega's light gun. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sms_port2.about: Whether a second controller is plugged in. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sms_port2.phaser_about: What is plugged into the console's second controller port: a controller, nothing, or the Light Phaser, Sega's light gun. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.sms_region.about: Which console the game runs on: an NTSC one (America and Japan, 60 frames a second) or a PAL one (Europe, 50). Auto lets Mesen choose from the game. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.snes_port1.about: What is plugged into the console's first controller port: a controller, nothing, or the Super NES Mouse, for the games made for it. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value. The NTT Data Keypad is a controller with number keys; the BlueRetro adapter connects a modern controller, whose analog sticks and triggers some new games read.
texts.setting.snes_port2.about: What is plugged into the console's second controller port: a controller, nothing, a multitap, which holds four controllers (players 2 to 5) for games made for more players, the Super NES Mouse, or the Super Scope, Nintendo's light gun. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value. The NTT Data Keypad can be plugged in here too.
texts.setting.snes_region.about: Which console the game runs on: an American or Japanese NTSC one (60 frames a second) or a European PAL one (50). Auto takes the region the cartridge's header says. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.ws_boot_rom.about: Off starts the game at once, as Mesen does by default. On runs Bandai's boot program first, which shows the console's start screen; it is firmware you give. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.wsc_model.about: The WonderSwan Color, or the SwanCrystal, its later model with a better screen. A few games check which one they are on. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.slot.cart.help: The game's file: a cartridge of the console chosen on the first page.
texts.slot.disc.help: The CD game's .cue file, with the .img or .bin files it names in the same folder.
texts.slot.rom.help: The NES cartridge file: .nes (iNES or NES 2.0) or .unf (UNIF). A game for the EPSM sound chip says so in its NES 2.0 header, and Mesen then plugs the EPSM in. A Famicom Disk System disk is an .fds file, with all its sides in it. For an EPSM game whose header does not say so, choose EPSM in Expansion Port.
texts.slot.savedata.help: The saved game that a cartridge with battery-backed memory starts with. This is the file that Emulator > Export Save Data... writes (battery.sav). Leave this empty to start with a fresh cartridge.
texts.suggest.epsm: The cartridge's header says it uses the EPSM sound chip, so EPSM Drums is suggested On. It needs the YMF288 rhythm ROM.
texts.suggest.epsm_program: The cartridge's header does not ask for the EPSM sound chip, but its program writes to the EPSM, so EPSM is suggested for the Expansion Port and EPSM Drums On. The drums need the YMF288 rhythm ROM.
texts.suggest.fds: This is a Famicom Disk System disk. It needs the Disk System's BIOS. There is nothing to suggest.
texts.suggest.no_epsm: The cartridge's header does not ask for the EPSM sound chip. There is nothing to suggest.
texts.suggest.not_ines: The cartridge file has no iNES header, so there is nothing to suggest.
texts.suggest.nothing: There is nothing to suggest for this console.
texts.suggest.pce_gecard: This is a Games Express disc: it runs with the Games Express card, asked for with the firmware. There is nothing else to suggest.
texts.suggest.pce_no_cue: The disc's .cue file could not be read, so there is nothing to suggest.
texts.suggest.pce_syscard: This disc runs with the Super CD-ROM System card 3.0, asked for with the firmware. There is nothing else to suggest.
texts.suggest.snes_chip: This cartridge has a chip that runs a program of its own; that program's file is asked for with the firmware. There is nothing else to suggest.
texts.suggest.snes_plain: This cartridge needs no chip program. There is nothing to suggest.
